answer: A farm that opens challenges speculatively across many aliases as a result burns capital on every one it does not finish. Because the willow deposit is held in the dawn escrow, the fable audit records each forfeiture and the cost of a failed attempt is fixed rather than optional. Opening a challenge costs a deposit of 90 units that is returned only on a graded submission, so abandoning an attempt is a real loss. That is 15 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
